_comment: Shared expectations for the contact-matching ladder, exercised by BOTH
The ladder is implemented twice (Python for the eval's FakeDevice, Kotlin on the
device) and this file is what stops the two drifting apart unnoticed.
These cases pin CURRENT behaviour, including behaviour that is arguably wrong -
cases tagged "sharp_edge" are recorded so a future change to them is a deliberate
decision with a failing test, not an accident.

cases.why: An exact name match wins over a longer name that merely starts with it.
A name starting with the needle wins over one merely containing it.
needle.startsWith(name) counts as a prefix match, so a short stored name absorbs a longer spoken one. Loose, but load-bearing when a contact is saved by first name only.
The contains tier is guarded at 3 characters so short fragments cannot match half the address book.
At exactly 3 characters the contains tier engages.
A number is used directly, with spaces stripped, without touching the address book.
Digits are treated as a number even when contacts exist.
An unknown name resolves to nothing, so the caller can ask rather than guess.
Stored numbers have spaces stripped before use.

Two contacts tie on the prefix tier and the first seen wins. On-device that order comes from the ContentResolver cursor, so which of two equally-good contacts is picked is not actually deterministic. Recorded here to make the ambiguity visible; resolving it properly means asking the user.
An empty name must not match anyone. Both implementations used to return the first contact, because every name startsWith("").
Same as the empty case after trimming.
A contact missing a name or a number is not a candidate.
